verdict.rationale: Open WebUI's first-party Computer ecosystem gives the AI a real exec surface on the user's machine. It connects to your real files, and the approval mode gates when "something changes on disk" or a "command runs". Supervision cards show every file read and edit, and scheduled tasks can run the test suite. Missing for 10: detailed docs on the shell/command tool's scope and sandboxing on the host, and independent hands-on corroboration of command execution and file editing.

support.subject: As a power user, the assistant can run commands and edit files on my machine — a real exec surface, not just chat about what to do

citations.quote: auto is the everyday setting: the AI can explore freely, but nothing changes on disk and no command runs until you say so.
You see the full history: every file it read, every edit it made, and the pending approval that's blocking it, rendered as tool cards with Allow / Deny buttons.
From zero to your real files in a browser, in about two minutes.
Run Python directly in the browser or via Open Terminal
Schedule a task that runs the test suite every weekday at 9 and reports failures with the error output.
